title: Surface Area of Revolution from Parametric Curve
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Find the surface area generated by revolving the semicircle x = R cos(t), y = R sin(t) for 0 <= t <= pi about the x-axis.

steps.title: Compute Speed Factor
steps.mathExpression: x' = -R\sin t, \; y' = R\cos t \implies \sqrt{(x')^2 + (y')^2} = \sqrt{R^2(\sin^2 t + \cos^2 t)} = R
steps.explanation: Constant speed R along circular path.

steps.title: Set Up Surface Area Integral
steps.mathExpression: S = 2\pi \int_0^\pi y(t) \sqrt{(x')^2 + (y')^2} dt = 2\pi \int_0^\pi (R\sin t)(R) dt = 2\pi R^2 \int_0^\pi \sin(t) dt
